core_obligations: Base cases (proof lines 2909-2918): choose an element mapping to a uniformizer and write the kernel of the surjection minimally as generated by the remaining elements; if there are only two generators then the maximal ideal is generated by two elements and the ring is already regular, and in general after renumbering one may assume that one of the generators maps to a uniformizer of the local ring at the kernel prime.

Produce relations for the generators (proof lines 2918-2936): the quotient of the kernel by the square plus the chosen generator is annihilated by a power of the uniformizer, so for each remaining generator there is an integer and an element of the ring such that a product of the uniformizer power with the generator differs from a multiple of the chosen generator by an element of the square of the kernel; if for some generator the exponent vanishes or the multiplier is a unit, that generator or the chosen one can be removed and the argument concludes by induction on the number of generators; otherwise each multiplier lies in the kernel or is a unit times a power of the uniformizer.

Blow up and let the exponents decrease (proof lines 2938-2950): passing to the affine blowup algebra the generators of the base are recovered by the quotients over the uniformizer, and the displayed relations transform into the same shape with both relevant exponents decreased by one; hence blowing up in the point of the arc repeatedly decreases these integers, which cannot continue indefinitely, so at some stage the exponents vanish or a multiplier becomes a unit and the induction terminates, giving that one of the blowups is regular at the point of the arc.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a minimal generating set of the kernel and dispose of the cases with two generators.
Derive relations exhibiting the obstruction as powers of the uniformizer and discard generators when possible.
Show that blowing up decreases the exponents, so the process must terminate and a term of the sequence is regular there.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a two dimensional Noetherian local domain with a surjection onto a complete discrete valuation ring defining a nonsingular arc, if the local ring at the kernel prime is regular then one of the blowups in the sequence determined by the arc is regular at the point of the arc (statement lines 2896-2909). The proof (proof lines 2911-2954) works with a minimal generating set of the kernel, derives relations controlled by powers of a uniformizer, and shows that passing to the affine blowup algebra strictly decreases the relevant exponents, forcing termination. H3: an original termination argument with explicit blowup computations, written out in full.
